chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Harun ibn Muslim, from Mas'adah ibn Sadah, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
"Circumcise your children at the age of seven, for it is purer and faster for the growth of the flesh. Indeed, the earth dislikes the urine of the uncircumcised."
ai.seo_question: What is the recommended age and rationale for circumcision in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) establishes the recommended age of seven for circumcision, linking physical hygiene to spiritual cleanliness. The narration highlights the natural aversion of the earth to the urine of the uncircumcised (al-aghlaaf), a concept often interpreted in Shia jurisprudence as reflecting both biological efficiency in waste elimination and a symbolic purity that aligns with the Fitrah (innate disposition). This ruling underscores the integration of bodily care with religious observance, emphasizing that physical cleanliness is a precursor to spiritual readiness.
